skill.name: linear-cli
skill.description: Manage Linear issues, projects, documents, and status updates through documented CLI workflows and GraphQL queries.
skill.summary: Use Linear CLI commands to track work, update issues, and coordinate projects.
skill.author: schpet

security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown formatting, TypeScript strings, or legitimate Linear commands rather than execution, obfuscation, credential-file access, or reconnaissance. Confirmed risks concern predictable shared temporary files and authentication tokens exposed through curl arguments. No evidence found of prompt injection or intentional exfiltration in the reviewed source; the external CLI implementation was not audited.

remediation.issue: Examples write and consume predictable filenames in shared temporary directories.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private mktemp directory with restrictive permissions, verify file ownership, and remove temporary files after use in both skill documents.

remediation.issue: The curl example expands the authentication token into process arguments, where local process inspection or tracing may expose it.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer linear api. When curl is necessary, supply authentication through protected input rather than arguments, disable shell tracing, and redact credentials from logs.

content.user_title: Manage Linear Work from the Command Line
content.value_statement: Maintaining issues and project updates across separate interfaces takes time. This skill gives your assistant documented Linear CLI workflows for finding work and applying requested changes.
actual_capabilities: Query issues by team, project, state, assignee, labels, and dates, with structured output where supported.
Create issues and update their status, assignee, labels, cycle, milestone, or description.
Add Markdown comments, threaded replies, inline image attachments, and plain Linear URL mentions.
Manage projects, initiatives, documents, and their comments or status updates.
Browse templates and apply issue or project templates during creation.
Inspect the GraphQL schema and make authenticated API requests when dedicated commands do not cover an operation.
limitations: Requires an available Linear CLI, network access, and credentials authorized for the target workspace.
Provides instructions and references, not the Linear CLI implementation or an independent project management service.
Command availability and behavior depend on the installed CLI version and Linear API.
Document templates cannot be applied through the API; project descriptions have a 255-character limit.

use_cases.title: Track Development Work
use_cases.description: Find assigned issues, review requirements, and update issue status while working from the terminal.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Project Delivery
use_cases.description: Review project issues, maintain milestones, and publish approved project or initiative status updates.

use_cases.title: Document Reproducible Bugs
use_cases.description: Create issues from team templates and attach screenshots with formatted reproduction steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Active Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: List my started issues in team [TEAM], ordered by priority. Summarize each issue without changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Bug Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the Bug report template for team [TEAM]. Draft an issue titled [TITLE] using [REPRODUCTION_STEPS], then ask for approval before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Project Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Review issues for project [PROJECT]. Draft a status update covering completed work and blockers. Ask for approval before publishing it.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Read-Only API Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve [REQUESTED_FIELDS] from workspace [WORKSPACE]. Check dedicated CLI commands first, then inspect the schema if GraphQL is necessary. Use read-only requests and never display credentials.

output_examples.input: Show an example summary of my active ENG issues.
output: ENG-123: Fix login redirect. High priority. In Progress.
ENG-128: Improve error messages. Normal priority. In Progress.

output_examples.input: Show an example project update draft for Mobile App.
output: Completed: Login validation and error message review.
Blocker: Release testing awaits a device compatibility decision.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, team, and target identifiers before mutations; obtain explicit approval for deletion, bulk changes, and public uploads.
Use private temporary files for multiline Markdown, restrict their permissions, and remove them after use.
Prefer dedicated CLI commands, use authenticated API fallback only when needed, and keep tokens out of arguments and logs.
anti_patterns: Using issue list for team-wide searches; it lists your issues, while issue query supports broader filters.
Replacing all labels when only an incremental change is intended, or archiving issues without an explicit request.
Uploading confidential attachments publicly or placing credentials and sensitive Markdown in shared temporary files.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when command execution and the required CLI are available.

faq.question: Do I need to install Linear CLI separately?
faq.answer: Yes, or use the documented npx alternative. Review the package source and version before executing downloaded software.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: Use Linear CLI authentication for your workspace. Its references describe system keyring storage and migration from plaintext credentials.

faq.question: Can this skill change or delete workspace data?
faq.answer: Yes. Documented commands create, update, archive, and delete resources within your permissions. Confirm targets and approve destructive operations.

faq.question: Can screenshots appear inside comments?
faq.answer: Yes. Comment attachments render images inline. Issue attachments create sidebar links instead; public uploads require explicit approval.

faq.question: What happens when no dedicated command covers my request?
faq.answer: The skill documents schema inspection and authenticated GraphQL requests. These still require valid credentials and appropriate workspace permissions.
